subsections.subtitle: Core Mechanics
changes: Characters now have a detailed anatomical structure.
Body parts can take damage, lose functionality, or be destroyed.
Vital body parts (e.g., Head, Torso) cause death if lost.
Limb loss affects combat (e.g., losing a hand means dropping weapons).
NPCs generate with appropriate anatomy based on their Race and BodyType.
AnatomyGenerator and NPCGenerator ensure correct anatomy assignment upon creation.
NPCs now correctly generate with full anatomy upon creation, including camp NPCs.
Anatomy-based equipment validation ensures characters can only equip items if they have the required body parts.
Equipment slots are dynamically assigned based on body structure (e.g., missing limbs prevent certain items from being equipped).
Anatomy data includes hierarchical body part relationships, allowing for complex damage effects.

subsections.subtitle: Damage & Targeting Changes
changes: Damage now targets individual body parts instead of overall health.
Lost limbs impact gameplay (e.g., dropping weapons when a hand is lost).
Critical hits can destroy body parts outright.
Resistance now applies per body part, affecting damage mitigation.
All combat logic now centralized in Character.cs for efficiency.
Magic and physical attacks now use unified damage calculations.

subsections.subtitle: Combat Messaging & Feedback
changes: Detailed combat messages explain exactly what happens.
Messages log to both the console and in-game combat log.
Ensures clearer battle feedback for players.

subsections.subtitle: Item Handling
changes: Weapons, shields, and gear are unequipped and dropped when losing a body part.
Fixed duplication issue—items are now removed from the character before being dropped.
Dropped items correctly appear on the ground and can be picked up by others.
NPCs now verify anatomy before equipping gear to prevent invalid equipment assignments.
Equipped items are now dropped when a corresponding body part is lost (e.g., losing an arm drops a held weapon).
Loadout generation now accounts for body type limitations (e.g., a race with no legs won't receive leg armor).
Inventory UI now properly reflects anatomy-based equipment slots, preventing equipping in unavailable slots.

subsections.subtitle: Resource Optimization
changes: Bitwise Flags are now assigned to map cells, improving resource and environment categorization.
ResourceTags support multi-category tagging, allowing cells to belong to multiple types.
GoldOre is now tagged as both Ore and PreciousStone for better filtering.
Improves performance in resource lookups and filtering.

subsections.subtitle: Water & Terrain Enhancements
changes: WaterLevel System (0-100) tracks underground moisture.
Cells now have subterranean water based on proximity to surface water bodies.
Underground water pockets introduced for future well and aquifer use.
SubterraneanTerrain now reflects actual water presence, not just WaterLevel.

subsections.subtitle: Cave System Improvements
changes: Caves are now generated underground instead of appearing on the surface.
Procedural generation ensures organic cave networks with connected tunnels.
Surface cave entrances now lead into underground tunnel systems.
Cave types now include Treasure Caves, Monster Lairs, Fungi Caves, Abandoned Camps, and Collapsed Tunnels.

subsections.subtitle: Expansion Mechanics
changes: Villages accumulate Expansion Points over time, influenced by Population size.
Villages assess nearby land for expansion based on resource availability, expansion cost, and strategic placement.
Villages can delay expansion if they lack the points for their preferred land.

subsections.subtitle: AI Expansion Behavior
changes: Villages now weight expansion choices instead of always selecting the optimal one.
Randomized weighting system allows for unexpected expansion decisions.
Villages prioritize adjacent expansion but will seek strategic advantages.

subsections.subtitle: Resource Storage & Consumption
changes: Villages now store Food, Water, Wood, and Stone separately from passive generation.
Food & Water decay if not replenished, scaling with population size.
High food levels increase Health over time.
Starvation & dehydration reduce Health and impact Population growth.

subsections.subtitle: Bitwise Flags & Resource Tagging
changes: Added Bitwise Flags for ResourceTags & EnvironmentalTags.
ResourceTags now support efficient multi-category tagging.
Allows cells to belong to multiple categories (e.g., GoldOre is both Ore and PreciousStone).
Improves performance in resource lookups & filtering.

subsections.subtitle: Village Stats & Expansion Improvements
changes: StoredFood, StoredWater, StoredWood, and StoredStone added to VillageStats.
FoodGain, WaterGain, WoodGain, and StoneGain now increase periodically.
Expansion cost now factors in racial expansion preferences.

subsections.subtitle: Refactoring & Fixes
changes: Refactored Cell Resource Tagging for better efficiency.
Updated MapGenerator resource assignments to correctly apply parent categories.
Fixed Expansion Cost retrieval errors.

subsections.subtitle: Introduction of Monsters
changes: Monsters now exist as a distinct entity in the game, separate from NPCs.
Monster class introduced with unique properties, behaviors, and AI logic.
Monster generation logic integrated into the world, allowing for proper dungeon spawning.

subsections.subtitle: Undead Monsters & Boss Variants
changes: Skeletons and Zombies now spawn in dungeons, with Skeleton Lords and Dread Zombies serving as boss variants.
Boss monsters have enhanced stats, unique abilities, and better loot tables.
Monster attributes include health, strength, speed, awareness, and resistances.

subsections.subtitle: Monster Placement & Spawning
changes: Monsters now spawn dynamically in dungeons based on level and type.
MonsterManager handles placement logic to ensure valid, passable spawn points.
Boss monsters are placed separately at the lowest dungeon level.

subsections.subtitle: Loot System Integration
changes: Monsters now drop loot upon death, including weapons, armor, and crafting materials.
Boss monsters have higher-quality loot, with a chance for enhanced equipment.
Loot rarity scales with monster level.

subsections.subtitle: Monster Remains
changes: Monsters now leave behind remains (e.g., 'Skeleton Remains' or 'Zombie Remains').
Remains act as a loot container, storing any dropped items.
Boss remains persist longer and have unique descriptions.
Monster level is stored in remains for future interactions (e.g., necromancy or scavenging).

subsections.subtitle: Monster Inspection
changes: Players can now inspect monsters to view their health, type, and attributes.
Inspection UI updated to display monster stats clearly.
Boss monsters have special inspection messages indicating their status.

subsections.subtitle: Combat Integration
changes: Monsters participate in combat using the same anatomical damage system as NPCs.
Combat log now correctly tracks damage dealt to monsters.
Monsters correctly die when vital body parts are destroyed.
